risks.claim: The Christmas Spectacular production represented 18% of the company's revenues in Fiscal Year 2026, and the company's own risk disclosure states that a decline in its popularity 'could have a material negative effect on our business and results of operations.'
quotes: The financial results of our business are dependent on the Christmas Spectacular production, for which the 2025 production represented 18% of our revenues in Fiscal Year 2026.

The popularity of the Christmas Spectacular has in the past declined, for example, as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, and if it were to decline in the future (including, for example, due to an economic downturn or another pandemic or other public health emergency), our revenues from ticket sales and concession and merchandise sales would decline, possibly materially as they did during the COVID-19 pandemic, and we might not be able to replace the lost revenue with revenues from other sources.

risks.basis: Stated directly in P6 8-K; the specific overlap counts and roles are explicitly listed.
risks.claim: The company's Executive Chairman and CEO James L. Dolan simultaneously serves as Executive Chairman and CEO of Sphere Entertainment, MSG Knickerbockers, and MSG Rangers, and as Non-Executive Chairman of AMC Global Media, with eight of MSGE's directors also serving on Sphere Entertainment's board, creating 'actual or apparent conflicts of interest.'
quotes: The Company's Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, James L. Dolan, also serves as the Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Sphere Entertainment, MSG Knickerbockers and MSG Rangers and as Non-Executive Chairman of AMC Global Media.

eight of the Company's directors also serve as directors of Sphere Entertainment, seven of the Company's directors also serve as directors of MSG Knickerbockers, four of the Company's directors also serve as directors of MSG Rangers and three of the Company's directors also serve as directors of AMC Global Media.

The overlapping directors and officers may have actual or apparent conflicts of interest with respect to matters involving or affecting the Company, on the one hand, and Sphere Entertainment, MSG Knickerbockers, MSG Rangers or AMC Global Media, on the other hand.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 Risk Factors; the lease expiry dates and net-worth requirement are explicitly described. The thin equity figure is from F1.
risks.claim: Radio City Music Hall and the Beacon Theatre are leased rather than owned, with leases expiring in 2036 and 2038 respectively, and the guarantor entity for the Radio City Music Hall lease must maintain a certain net worth or face a requirement to post a letter of credit or cash collateral.
quotes: We lease the Beacon Theatre and Radio City Music Hall under long-term leases that expire in 2036 and 2038, respectively.

MSG Entertainment Holdings, the entity that guarantees the lease for Radio City Music Hall, is also required to maintain a certain net worth that, if not maintained, would require the entity to post a letter of credit or provide cash collateral.
If MSG Entertainment Holdings were to breach or become unable to satisfy this obligation, we could suffer operational difficulties and/or significant losses.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 Risk Factors; the competitive language and artist-dependency risk are the company's own disclosure.
risks.claim: The company's business is 'highly sensitive to customer tastes and depends on our ability to attract artists and events,' and the risk disclosure notes 'there may be a limited number of popular artists, groups or events that can attract audiences to our venues.'
quotes: In addition, our business is highly sensitive to customer tastes and depends on our ability to attract artists and events.

There may be a limited number of popular artists, groups or events that can attract audiences to our venues, and our business would suffer to the extent that we are unable to continue to attract such artists, groups or events to perform at our venues.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors, filed 2026-08-14); the MOU is explicitly described as non-binding.
unresolved_questions.claim: What are the final financial terms of the transfer of the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden to the Master Developer, and will the transaction be completed?
quotes: On June 8, 2026, in connection with the proposed redevelopment of Penn Station, the Company announced it had entered into a non-binding memorandum of understanding with the Master Developer, which was previously selected by The National Railroad Passenger Corporation ("Amtrak") to redevelop Penn Station, subject to the execution of various binding agreements (the "Developer Agreements"), contemplating the transfer of the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden to the Master Developer

There can be no assurance that the redevelopment of Penn Station or the transactions involving the Company, Amtrak and the Master Developer described above (including the transfer of the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden) will be completed on the terms described above, or at all.

unresolved_questions.claim: How do the Arena License Agreements operate after the distribution of MSG Rangers Corp. from MSG Knickerbockers Corp., and are the 35-year terms running through 2055 unchanged?
quotes: Following the distribution by MSG Knickerbockers Corp. (formerly Madison Square Garden Corp. and referred to herein as "MSG Knickerbockers") of all of the issued and outstanding shares of the common stock of MSG Rangers Corp. (formerly MSGS Spinco, Inc. and referred to herein as "MSG Rangers") to its stockholders (the "MSG Rangers Distribution")

Under the Arena License Agreements, which each have a term of 35 years running through 2055, the Knicks and the Rangers pay an annual license fee in connection with their respective use of The Garden.

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors); the specific renewal terms are not yet determined.
unresolved_questions.claim: What are the terms and conditions of the upcoming renewal of The Garden's zoning special permit, which was last renewed in September 2023 for five years?
quotes: The Garden requires a zoning special permit, which was originally granted by the New York City Planning Commission in 1963 and most recently renewed in September 2023 for five years.

There can be no assurance regarding the future renewal of the special permit or the terms thereof (including requirements for us to make significant capital expenditures as a condition to renewal of the permit), and the failure to obtain such renewal or to do so on favorable terms would have a material negative effect on our business.
